names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 24 aprilie, «Sfântul Mucenic Valentin din Durostorum».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 24 Απριλίου, «Άγιοι Πασικράτης και Βαλεντίων», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог's heading for 24. април ст. ст., „Св. муч. Пасикрат и Валентин.“, with „Св.“ and the one rank word муч., which stands over both names, left off. The heading gives no city and the body says nothing of him beyond the beheading; Durostorum is the Greek calendar's. No other folder in this corpus holds this form — `valentina-of-caesarea`'s Russian «Валентина Кесарийская» is a woman's name and a fuller form.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 24 aprilie — «Sfântul Mucenic Valentin din Durostorum»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 24ης Απριλίου — «Άγιοι Πασικράτης και Βαλεντίων»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 24 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing and the same day the Romanian calendar keeps them. The Greek makes them soldiers of Durostorum in Lower Moesia under a prefect Aulozanes, arrested for rebuking the worshippers of the idols and for confessing Christ true God, urged to sacrifice to Apollo, and beheaded in 297 — Passicrates at twenty-two, Valention at thirty; it adds the scene of Passicrates's brother coming to the prison and advising him to offer at least a little incense and save himself, and Passicrates driving him off. **This folder had no `dates` and now has both years**, taken from the page's headings «Αγιος Βαλεντιων (267 - 297)» and «Αγιος Πασικρατης (275 - 297)», which are the ages the text gives worked back from 297. The day's line spells the second name Βαλεντίων, and the corpus's English form is Valentine. It prints no hymn and names no relic.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 07.05.2026 (24. април ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Пасикрат и Валентин.“

attestations.note: A SECOND DAY ON THIS CHURCH, ADDED 5 October 2026. **THE BOOK CONTRADICTS ITSELF ACROSS ITS OWN TWO DAYS, AND BY SEVENTY-FOUR YEARS.** `BRIEF.md` §4 allows a reader to write a second-day note on a row that is already `venerated`, under `replace_venerated: true`, and **the row is copied back byte for byte** — same day, same month, same source, same year — **with the note added and nothing else changed**. The Prologue keeps this man **twice**: on the Julian 24 April, headed „Св. муч. Пасикрат и Валентин.“, where it says the two were beheaded together „око 228. год.“, and again here on the Julian 25 May, where it says the company suffered „око 302. године“. **It is the same pair and demonstrably so, because the same brother appears in both**: the apostate Папијан, who in the 24 April entry is urged on Pasicrates by the judge and in this one comes to him himself. **So this is not two men but one book with two answers**, which is the reading made for `basiliscus-of-amasea` on 22 May, where the Prologue’s own 3 March and 22 May entries told his death two ways. **No second row was made and no day was moved**: one attestation row per church is the schema, this church’s row stays on the Julian 24 April, and he does not render on the 25 May. **And `dates` is untouched.** The folder holds a `death` of 297 off doxologia and saint.gr; the Prologue’s two guesses, 228 and 302, straddle it, and widening to 228–302 on the strength of two approximations the same book makes against itself would put a seventy-four-year interval on the folder in place of a year two other calendars agree on. **It is recorded here and left for the author.** The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23, 24 and 25 May is. The 25 May heading is „Свети мученици Пасикрат, Валентион, Јулије и други“, which names him second, and the entry says of him exactly what the 24 April one says: **„Пасикрат и Валентион буду заједно посечени“**, the two beheaded together. **So this day adds nothing to his own story and everything to its setting**: the company of five, the place Durostorum, the year about 302, and the dialogue that belongs to the other four. That is itself the reading — **the Prologue is as silent about this man on its second day as on its first**, and the row is written so that a later reader does not take the 25 May entry for a different Valention. **He gains no new name form**: «Валентин» is stored off the 24 April heading, which prints „Валентин“, and **the 25 May heading prints „Валентион“, a different string** — `foldchk.py` returns `[('valentine-of-durostorum', 'sr')]` for the stored form and `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Валентион». **The second form is refused and this is a reading, not an oversight**: one `sr` form per folder, the fullest, and „Валентион“ is neither fuller nor a different name but the same name in the same book spelled two ways two days apart. Both spellings are named here so the next reader to meet „Валентион“ knows which folder holds it. **THREE NEW `related` ROWS, ALL RECIPROCAL**, on the same reading as his companion’s: the entry narrates one martyrdom for five men. `types` untouched, both corroborated. No `locations`. No hymn.

birth.note: saint.gr heads him «Αγιος Βαλεντίων (267 - 297)», and its text gives his age at death as thirty in the year 297.

death.note: saint.gr: «Τότε και οι δύο αποκεφαλίστηκαν, σε ηλικία, ο μεν Πασικράτης 22 ετών, ο δε Βαλεντίων 30, το έτος 297 μ.Χ.»
